answer: An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Because a fabricated citation fails the pearl check immediately, the terrace audit keeps the resolved set and the lotus replay makes public exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 166 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 166 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 31 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
